To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the free 1/25-dihydroxylated metabolite of vitamin D is a more accurate reflection of the biologic activity of the vitamin than is the total 1, 25-dihydroxlated metabolite in patients with nephrotic and renal failure.
the serum concentrations of total (r = 1.000) and free 1.25(OH) 2D (r = 974) decrease as renal function worsens in patients with renal disease.

in patients with renal disease, the serum concentrations of total, but not free, 1,25 dihydroxy vitamin D decrease with the worsening of renal failure, and that in patients on peritoneal diaylsis and in nephrotic patients with low serum levels of vitamin D binding protein (DBP), free 1, 25 dihydroxyvitamin D concentrations are higher than in normal subjects.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the measurement of 1, 25 dihydroxy vitamin D in patients with chronic renal failure.
the relationship between the free and total 1.25 dihydroxyvitamin D in patients with various stages of renal disease.
a study of the relationship between the serum levels of total and free (1,25(O2)D, and the serum levels of DBP in patients with various renal diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the free 1.25(OH)D is a better reflection of the 1.25 (OH)D activity than total 1.25(0H)D.
in the presence of renal disease, the measurement of total 1.25 (OH) 2D is an accurate reflection of 1.25(OH) 2D status, except in the presence of proteinuria.

in the setting of renal insufficiency, the measurement of total 1.25 (OH) 2D is a reliable index of 1, 25 (OH)2D status, whereas in the presence of nephrotic syndrome the measurement of free 1.25(OH) 2D may be required.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the free 1.25(OH)D fraction is the biologically active fraction of the hormone and is the best measure of 1.25D activity.

the total 1, 25 dihydroxyvitamin D level is a good reflection of the 1,25 dihydroxy status in patients with normal renal function, mild and moderate renal insufficiency, and in patients undergoing hemodialysis.
in patients with chronic kidney disease, the total and free 25-hydroxyvitamin-D levels are significantly lower than in healthy controls.
The main takeaway from our work is that
in patients on peritoneal and hemodialysis, the free fraction is a more accurate representation of the true activity of vitamin D.
in subjects with nephrotics syndrome and varying degrees in renal failure including those on chronic hemodialysis, may have the low serum concentrations of the total 1, 25-dihydrovitamin D.

the total 1, 25 dihydroxyvitamin D level is a good reflection of vitamin D status in normal subjects and patients with renal insufficiencies, but in patients with nephrotic range proteinuria or on peritoneal or hemodialysis the free 1.25 dihydroxy vitamin D level should be measured to get a better picture of vitamin D status.
